newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-PAULUS PICKS UP WIN, POINTS AT PHILADELPHIA TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PAULUS PICKS UP WIN, POINTS AT PHILADELPHIA TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Austrian Barbara Paulus, the only seeded player in action on Monday at the $450,000 Advanta Championship, convincingly defeated South African Amanda Coetzer 6-1 6-2 in their first-round match.
The victory was an important one for Paulus, who is 16th on the Corel WTA Tour points list heading into next week's year-ending championships at Madison Square Garden.
The top 16 points-getters and one alternate qualify, and Coetzer is ranked 14th but could be passed this week by Paulus and Mary Joe Fernandez, who is also playing here.
Paulus, seeded eighth in the field of 32, breezed through the first set before Coetzer won the first two games of the second set. Paulus then won the next six games to close out the match.
"For me this is not a warmup tournament," Paulus said. "I "I have to make some points in this tournament."
In other matches, Americans Chanda Rubin, Amy Frazier, Marianne Werdel Witmeyer and Meghann Shaughnessy advanced to the second round with victories.
Rubin dropped the first set before rallying to defeat Spain's Virginia Ruano-Pascual 4-6 6-1 7-5, while Frazier, ranked 28th in the world, defeated Karina Habsudova of Slovakia 7-6 (7-4) 6-4.
Frazier's second-round opponent on Wednesday will be top seed and defending champion Steffi Graf, who re-entered the tournament Sunday after withdrawing Saturday due to an injured left knee.
The 114th-ranked Werdel Witmeyer beat Radka Zrubakova, also of Slovakia, and Shaughnessy, a wild-card entrant, defeated fellow American Laxmi Poruri 3-6 6-2 6-2.
